mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is a continuous predictor of S&P 500 60-day forward returns. A lower FEDFUNDS level is associated with positive returns due to compressed discount rates, and the relationship is monotonic such that the signal always predicts positive returns regardless of absolute rate levels.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in more than 10% of monthly observations where FEDFUNDS is reported.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals impending monetary policy response (rate cuts), compressing discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 30% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an imminent recession, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO declines >1% and UNRATE rises >0.2% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), higher discount rates and reduced liquidity produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 30% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of real GDP (GDPC1) is a continuous predictor of S&P 500 60-day forward returns. A higher GDP growth rate (as measured by quarterly change) is associated with positive returns due to stronger corporate earnings growth, and the relationship is monotonic such that the signal always predicts positive returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in more than 10% of quarterly observations where GDPC1 is reported.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 30% of instances where HOUST falls below 1200.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decline in residential sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a severe housing market contraction, which is a leading indicator of recession and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS declines >2% and HOUST declines >1.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is a continuous predictor of S&P 500 5-day forward returns. The relationship is such that the signal always predicts positive returns regardless of absolute CPI levels due to market expectations of inflation-targeting policy responses.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of monthly observations where CPIAUCSL is reported.
